readings: Whoever does the will of God lives forever

theo: After Simeon comes Anna, a prophet, the daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher, a widow of great age. She “never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.” A whole life of faithful prayer prepares her to recognise the child at once. She becomes one of the first evangelists: she praises God and speaks about the child to everyone waiting for redemption.

Luke places a man and a woman, Simeon and Anna, side by side as witnesses; both elderly, both full of the Spirit. The elderly have a mission in the Church: to pray, to remember and to pass on the faith (Pope Francis, catecheses on old age, 2022). The first reading warns that “the world and its desire are passing away, but those who do the will of God live forever.” Then the Holy Family returns to Nazareth, and “the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom”.

family.intention: We pray for widows and elderly people who live alone.

pm.open: Lord God, Anna praised you when she saw the Child. As we gather near the end of the year, teach us to love your will above the passing things of the world. Amen.
share: John says the world is passing away (1 John 2:17). What passing things take too much of my heart?
Anna turned loneliness into prayer (Luke 2:37). How do I handle loneliness?
Whom can I tell about Jesus this Christmas season?
pm.resp: Those who do the will of God live for ever.
interc: For the Church, that her members of every age may grow in faith.
For widows and the elderly, that they may find comfort and community.
For young people, that they may conquer the evil one.
For those attached to riches and pleasures, that they may find true life.
For our group, that we may grow in wisdom and grace.
pm.close: Lord God, Anna waited and prayed and saw your salvation. Free us from love of passing things, and make us faithful in prayer until we see you face to face. Amen.

illus: A widow in Muvattupuzha has attended the 6 a.m. Mass every day for thirty years since her husband died. The young people call her “our Anna.” She says: “I am never alone. I have the whole parish in my prayers.”

homily: Dear friends, St John writes to Christians of every age: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven; to you, fathers, because you know him; to you, young people, because you have conquered the evil one (1 John 2:12–14). Every generation has its place in God's family.

Then he warns: do not love the world or the things in the world. The desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, the pride in riches, comes not from the Father. The world and its desire are passing away, but those who do the will of God live for ever (1 John 2:15–17).

In the Gospel we meet Anna, a prophet, eighty-four years old, a widow who never left the Temple but worshipped there with fasting and prayer night and day. At that moment she came, began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem (Luke 2:36–38).
Anna was a widow for most of her life. She could have become bitter. Instead, she made her loneliness into prayer. And because she was praying, she was there at the right moment to meet the Messiah.
Then the Gospel says: the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom; and the favour of God was upon him (Luke 2:40). The Son of God grew up slowly, in an ordinary home in Nazareth.

At the end of this year, let us examine what we love: the passing things of the world, or the will of God that lasts for ever? Let us honour the widows and elderly in our parish, and learn from Anna to turn loneliness into prayer and praise. Amen.
kids: Children, Anna was very old and prayed every day. Thank God for your grandparents who pray for you!

intro: Anna's faithful prayer, her joyful witness, and the quiet growth of Jesus at Nazareth.

sub: Fasting and prayer night and day.
q: even to your old age I am he, even when you turn gray I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save.

There was also a prophet, Anna the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was of a great age, having lived with her husband seven years after her marriage, then as a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.

When they had finished everything required by the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth. The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom; and the favor of God was upon him.

The world passes; God's will remains.
